title: Gargantua and Pantagruel
published_date: c. 1532-1564 (composite chronology not re-verified this session; digital compilation verified)

access.edition_or_version: Composite English text (translations by Thomas Urquhart and Peter Anthony Motteux) via Project Gutenberg ebook #1200; Gutenberg RDF title 'Gargantua and Pantagruel' verified 2026-09-24
access.translator: Thomas Urquhart and Peter Anthony Motteux

mechanics.premise: Two giants — father and son — live, learn, war, and feast through picaresque adventures that cartwheel across courts, churches, and schools.
mechanics.deflation_targets: Knights, churchmen, and scholastic authorities punctured through the giants' bodies — appetite, excretion, and excess answer every claim to dignity with material fact (Bakhtin-mediated reading; chapter-level attribution unverified).
mechanics.licensed_frame: The carnival/festival license Bakhtin locates in the work: comic anarchy bounded by frame, the lofty brought down temporarily, ordinary hierarchy resuming after (p. 10 paragraph verified; deeper locators unverified).
mechanics.point_of_view: Picaresque sprawl narrated in exuberant mock-chronicle voice.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Scale comedy (giant bodies vs. human institutions); catalogs and exaggeration; debasement of the lofty into the material-bodily — described from the verified Bakhtin paragraph and standard description only, no passages consulted or reproduced.
mechanics.dialogue: Formal rhetoric (sermons, letters, disputes) repeatedly undercut by bodily consequence.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Exuberant licensed overflow — the cycle's pleasure is surplus rather than targeted indignation.
mechanics.boundaries_and_restraint: Reads toward satirical-literature wherever a clerical or scholastic target persists; the no-sustained-target voice claim (clm-tone-irreverent-no-sustained-target) is what keeps it on the irreverent side.
mechanics.conventions: Foundational carnival text of European comic fiction.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Establishes bodily debasement as a legitimate instrument against dignity — the template Bakhtin made canonical.
mechanics.critical_reception: Bakhtin's 1960s study made it the master text of carnivalesque comedy; the reception debate over Bakhtin's singular reading is recorded as evidence-incomplete (no source in this silo documents it).
mechanics.audience_reception: Endures as the emblem — for scholars, less continuously read — of sanctioned bodily irreverence.
